∀ {n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) {κ : ℝ} (hκ : 4 ≤ κ)
    (h : ℝ → ℝ) (hh : Measurable h)
    (hL1 : Integrable (fun O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ => h ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 0 < 3) hn⟩ : Fin n) (⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 0 < 3) hn⟩ : Fin n))) ((Measure.haarMeasure (⊤ : PositiveCompacts (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ))))),     (∫ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ,
      (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * Real.sqrt ((((κ + 1) / 2) • (1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) - ((κ - 1) / 4) • ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) + (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).transpose))).det *
        h ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 0 < 3) hn⟩ : Fin n) (⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 0 < 3) hn⟩ : Fin n)) ∂(Measure.haarMeasure (⊤ : PositiveCompacts (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ)))) =
      ((-1 : ℝ) ^ (n - 1) * (Real.sqrt κ - 1) ^ (n - 1) / (2 : ℝ) ^ n) *
        (∫ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ,
          ((Real.sqrt κ + 1) * ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 0 < 3) hn⟩ : Fin n) (⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 0 < 3) hn⟩ : Fin n)) - (Real.sqrt κ - 1)) *
            h ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 0 < 3) hn⟩ : Fin n) (⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 0 < 3) hn⟩ : Fin n)) ∂(Measure.haarMeasure (⊤ : PositiveCompacts (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ))))
approved_definition_context: Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ is the full real orthogonal group, with inherited finite matrix topology and its Borel sigma-algebra; both determinant signs are allowed. It is compact, nonempty and second countable, with those facts constructed internally.

The displayed Measure.haarMeasure constructor is the actual Haar law normalized on top, the entire compact group. IsProbabilityMeasure means total mass one. No arbitrary caller-supplied law or conditional distribution is substituted.

A finite index set S is also its finite subtype of indices. Matrix.submatrix along the two subtype inclusions is the principal submatrix; the empty determinant is one. Fin n indices start at zero. The explicit proof inside the first index constructs its membership from the dimension inequality.

Integrable is actual absolute Bochner L1 integrability under the displayed Borel measure; Measurable h is Borel measurability on the real line. The given L1 condition is on the composition with the displayed entry, not an assertion that h is globally bounded.

All matrices and scalars are real. Matrix multiplication, transpose and determinant have their usual finite-dimensional meanings. Scalar multiplication is entrywise, 1 is identity, and Real.sqrt is the nonnegative real square root. The anonymous statement fully expands the displayed precision formula.
